pub_landlady.text: Welcome to the State Pub, pet. It's a funny old place. The government bought up every pub and brewery in Carlisle in 1916, to stop the munitions girls and lads at Gretna fighting over a shift pint. They ran them until 1971.
Plain rooms, plain furniture and a rule that you couldn't be served 'treat' rounds. They wanted people drinking sensibly. It was the only English pub scheme run by a Ministry.

else.text: Another time. The questions aren't going anywhere, and neither is the carpet.

pub_regular.text: Cumberland sausage is a local pride, coiled in a ring and sold by the length, and it has its own protected name. I like the ring.
Don't cut it into links. It's meant to be eaten in the coil, like a bicycle chain, only better for you.
